chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from whoever mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Quran was revealed with grief, so recite it with grief.

key_terms.اقرءوه: Recite it — second person plural imperative commanding the addressees to recite the Quran
key_terms.الحزن: Grief, sorrow, sadness — used to describe both the spiritual weight of the Quran's revelation and the appropriate emotional state when reciting it
key_terms.نزل: Descended, was revealed — the technical term for divine revelation being sent down from God

ai.seo_question: How should the Quran be recited according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that the Quran was revealed in a context of grief and gravity, and thus it should be recited with a sorrowful, weighty tone. This hadith, narrated through the respected chain including Ali ibn Ibrahim and Ibn Abi Umayr, establishes the proper emotional disposition for Quranic recitation. The instruction reflects the Shia tradition that reciting the Quran with a mournful voice — rather than casual indifference — honors the gravity of divine revelation and its content, which includes warnings, lamentations, and calls to accountability.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from the one who mentioned it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The Quran came down with the grief, therefore recite it with the grief’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from those whom he has mentioned (in his book) from abu ‘Abd Allah who has said the following: “
The Holy Quran has come down with sadness, thus, you should read it with sadness.”
